questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Panchayati Raj System -- An Overview' refers to.
questions.a: The Panchayati Raj system is a three-tier structure of local self-government in rural India that brings democracy to the village level through elected councils.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Panchayati Raj System -- An Overview'.
questions.a: Power is decentralised to village-level institutions so that rural citizens can govern their own affairs and solve local problems.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Panchayati Raj System -- An Overview' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Introduction to Grassroots Democracy

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Gram Sabha -- The Village Assembly' refers to.
questions.a: The Gram Sabha is the general body of all adult voters registered in a village; it is the foundation of the Panchayati Raj system where villagers meet to discuss and approve local matters.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Gram Sabha -- The Village Assembly'.
questions.a: The Gram Sabha is a direct democracy in which every eligible villager can participate, making it the bedrock of rural self-government.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Gram Sabha -- The Village Assembly' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Gram Sabha

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Gram Panchayat -- The Village Council' refers to.
questions.a: The Gram Panchayat is the elected executive body at the village level responsible for implementing development programmes and providing basic services to the village.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Gram Panchayat -- The Village Council'.
questions.a: The Gram Panchayat is the executive arm of rural local government that turns the Gram Sabha's decisions into action.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Gram Panchayat -- The Village Council' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Gram Panchayat

concepts.title: Three-Tier Structure -- Gram, Block and Zila Levels

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Three-Tier Structure -- Gram, Block and Zila Levels' refers to.
questions.a: The Panchayati Raj system is organised in three tiers: the Gram Panchayat at the village level, the Panchayat Samiti at the block level, and the Zila Parishad at the district level.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Three-Tier Structure -- Gram, Block and Zila Levels'.
questions.a: Each tier handles problems at its own geographical scale, with the village tier closest to the people and the district tier coordinating wider development.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Three-Tier Structure -- Gram, Block and Zila Levels' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Structure of Panchayati Raj

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Functions of the Gram Panchayat' refers to.
questions.a: The Gram Panchayat performs civic functions for the village such as supplying drinking water, maintaining roads and drains, street lighting, sanitation and running welfare schemes.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Functions of the Gram Panchayat'.
questions.a: The Gram Panchayat provides the everyday services and development work that villagers need most directly.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Functions of the Gram Panchayat' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Functions of Gram Panchayat

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Elections to Panchayats' refers to.
questions.a: Panchayat elections are direct elections held every five years in which village voters choose their Panchs and Sarpanch, with seats reserved for women and marginalised groups.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Elections to Panchayats'.
questions.a: Regular, direct elections with reservations ensure that all sections of village society get representation in local government.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Elections to Panchayats' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Elections to Panchayats

concepts.title: Role of the Sarpanch and Panch

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Role of the Sarpanch and Panch' refers to.
questions.a: The Sarpanch is the elected head of the Gram Panchayat who leads meetings and represents the village, while Panchs are elected members who look after specific wards and assist in decision-making.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Role of the Sarpanch and Panch'.
questions.a: The Sarpanch and Panchs together form the executive team that runs the village council and serves the needs of the villagers.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Role of the Sarpanch and Panch' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Sarpanch and Panch

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Sources of Income for Panchayats' refers to.
questions.a: Gram Panchayats raise money from taxes on houses, water and property, fees for services, and grants received from state and central governments.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Sources of Income for Panchayats'.
questions.a: A Panchayat needs a steady income from local taxes and government grants to carry out its development and service work.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Sources of Income for Panchayats' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Sources of Income

concepts.title: Importance of Local Self-Government in Rural Areas

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Importance of Local Self-Government in Rural Areas' refers to.
questions.a: Local self-government in rural areas empowers villagers to manage their own affairs, solve local problems quickly and participate directly in democracy.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Importance of Local Self-Government in Rural Areas'.
questions.a: When villagers govern themselves through Panchayats, decisions are faster, more relevant and more inclusive than when made by distant authorities.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Importance of Local Self-Government in Rural Areas' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Importance of Local Self-Government

concepts.title: Computing Quorum and Seat Reservation in Panchayats

questions.q: Calculate the number of seats reserved for women if a Gram Panchayat has 10 seats and one-third are reserved.. Use the method 'Computing Quorum and Seat Reservation in Panchayats'. Work with: reservation_fraction = 0.25, reserved_seats = 24, total_seats = 25. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of general_seats.
questions.a: 1 units

questions.q: How many seats are reserved for women in a Panchayat of 12 seats with one-third reservation? Use the method 'Computing Quorum and Seat Reservation in Panchayats'. Work with: reservation_fraction = 0.8, reserved_seats = 3, total_seats = 150. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of general_seats.
questions.a: 147 units

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Computing Quorum and Seat Reservation in Panchayats' refers to.
questions.a: Panchayat rules require a minimum number of members (quorum) to hold a valid meeting and reserve a fixed fraction of total seats for women and marginalised groups.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Computing Quorum and Seat Reservation in Panchayats'.
questions.a: Using simple fractions and rounding, one can calculate how many seats in a Panchayat must be reserved for women or marginalised groups.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Computing Quorum and Seat Reservation in Panchayats', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: reserved_seats = round(total_seats * reservation_fraction)
